annotations.title: List the billing contexts a reader can count as recurring

description:
List the billing contexts a reader can count as recurring revenue over one window, each with what counting it would add. This is what the recurring-contexts card offers; it measures nothing `well_sum_invoices` did not already measure, but it does judge each context by the months it billed.

Each entry in `groups` is one billing context's revenue in the window: `context_key` (the id a selection is matched on), `label` (the context as the product writes it), `amounts` (one entry per currency, each already net of credit notes and never converted) and `count` (the invoices behind it). The named contexts are sorted biggest first in the currency that carries the most invoices, so the biggest decision reads first. A context whose window nets to nothing in every currency is NOT listed — counting it would add nothing, so it is not a choice. A context that nets NEGATIVE stays on the list: its credit notes outweighed its invoices, which is a real state, and hiding it would move the figure by an amount nobody saw.

**The last entry may be `context_key: "unclassified"`, labelled "No billing context".** It is the invoices whose `billing_context` is `null`: extraction fills the field rather than a billing system, so on most workspaces it holds most of the revenue. It is a choice like the others. A business that bills only subscriptions can count it as recurring; a business with one-off work usually cannot. When it is counted, apply it to the `well_sum_invoices` rows whose `billing_context` is `null` — no row carries the key itself. **State its amount whenever it is listed**, counted or not, because it is the part of the figure extraction could not describe.

`totals` is the sum of the groups' amounts per currency: the window's whole readable issued revenue. **This read converts nothing and never adds one currency to another.** The reader decides per context, so the choice needs no single total; convert once, in the arithmetic, at a rate you state.

`measured` is the read's own view on which contexts are recurring: each listed context is judged by the months it billed in the window, under the same schedule rule the subscription detector applies on the bank side — monthly, bimonthly, quarterly or yearly. `measured.contexts` carries every verdict (`cadence`, `missed_rule`, `months_billed`) so the answer can be checked, and `measured.policy` states the rule in one line for the answer to restate. This is a measurement of the invoices, not a fact about the reader's business — a retainer is recurring for one company and a one-off engagement for another — so the card stays open for a correction, and a pick the reader records replaces the measured set on the next call.

`recurring_contexts` is the set this call settled on, and `reuse_stored_choice: true` says the card asks nothing: the answer applies as it stands. `choice_source` names what settled it — `"recorded_pick"` when the pick this conversation recorded applies, `"measured"` when the cadence verdicts did. When `reuse_stored_choice` is false — a read cut short, or a context whose months the rows did not carry — the card asks as before and `recurring_contexts` is empty.

`invoice_basis` is the window's issued revenue under the applied set, ready for the arithmetic: `totals` and `monthly_average` per currency (the average divides by every month of the window, dark ones included), `per_month` the same per month, `months_in_window`, `months_with_revenue`, `invoice_count`, the `unclassified_count` and `unattributed_count` the sum reported, and `excluded` (`one_off` is the invoices under contexts not counted, `credit_notes` the ones netted into the figure, `unreadable_rows` the defective rows). `by_client` answers the value per client on the same basis — every issued invoice in the window, counted or not under the recurring rule — one line per client per currency, largest first, the rest folded into an `is_other` line whose `client_count` says how many. `by_client_truncated: true` means the client grouping hit its cap, so the folded line may hold more than `client_count` names.

Apply the answer this result already carries when `reuse_stored_choice` is true: keep only the `well_sum_invoices` rows whose `billing_context` is in `recurring_contexts`, reading `"unclassified"` as the rows whose `billing_context` is `null`, pass the same keys to `well_render_mrr` as `recurring_contexts`, and state `measured.policy` in one line when `choice_source` is `"measured"` — a recorded pick is the reader's own rule, so name the contexts it counted instead. An EMPTY `recurring_contexts` beside `reuse_stored_choice: true` is the verdict that nothing in the window recurs under the rule: say no recurring revenue was found, never render a zero, and ask nothing. When `reuse_stored_choice` is false the card asks: take the reader's answer from it — its Continue records the pick with `well_switch_workspace` as `recurring_contexts`, and you read it back with `well_wait_for_selection` (kind "recurring_contexts").

The window is whole months: `from` and `to` are both the first day of a month, YYYY-MM-01, `from` inclusive and `to` EXCLUSIVE. `window` echoes both back exactly as you sent them. When a comparison will be measured, read the list over BOTH windows, from the start of the earlier one to the end of this one, so a context that stopped billing between them is still offered.

`partial: true` means the aggregate was cut short: every amount here is a FLOOR, a context's real share can only be larger, and a choice made because a share looked small may not survive the full read. Say so before presenting the list as a basis for the decision. A cut-short read never settles the recurring set either: the verdicts stay in `measured` as evidence, and the card asks. `unreadable_rows` counts invoices whose net amount or currency could not be read at all; they are in no figure here. It is `null` when that count could not be read, which is not zero: say it is unmeasured.

Read `party_scope`: when `party_scope.side_unknown` is true the workspace has no resolved own company, so no side filter was applied and the list covers invoices on both sides, purchase invoices included. Say the side is unknown and never offer the list as recurring revenue; resolve the own company, then list again.

Read `success` before `groups`: a failed read returns no contexts, which looks exactly like a window with nothing to choose.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window: the first day of a month, YYYY-MM-01.

to.description: EXCLUSIVE end of the window: the first day of the month after the last one you want, YYYY-MM-01.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_list_recurring_contexts

choice_source.description: What settled `recurring_contexts`: the pick this conversation recorded, or the cadence the read measured. Null when the card still asks.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

by_client.description: The value per client on the same issued-invoice basis — every invoice in the window, counted or not under the recurring rule. One line per client per currency, largest first; the rest fold into one `is_other` line per currency.

amount.description: The client's issued total over the window, net of credit notes, in `currency`.

client_count.description: On an `is_other` line, how many clients it sums.

is_other.description: Present on the rolled-up line that sums the clients too small to name.

per_month.description: `amount` divided by every month of the window.

by_client_truncated.description: True when the client grouping hit its cap: the folded line may hold more than `client_count` names, so say the list is partial.

excluded.description: What fell out of the figure, as three invoice counts kept apart.

credit_notes.description: Credit notes netted into the figure.

one_off.description: Issued invoices under a context not counted.

unreadable_rows.description: Invoices with no readable net amount or currency. Null when unmeasured.

invoice_count.description: Issued invoices in the window, counted or not.

monthly_average.description: `totals` divided by every month of the window — the figure an MRR reports, per currency.

months_in_window.description: Every month of the window — the divisor the average used.

months_with_revenue.description: Months holding at least one invoice of the applied set.

per_month.description: The applied set's net revenue per month, every window month once in order. A dark month carries an empty `amounts`.

totals.description: The applied set's net revenue over the window, one entry per currency it carries, never converted.

unattributed_count.description: Invoices Well could place on neither side, reported beside the figure rather than inside it. Null when unmeasured.

unclassified_count.description: Invoices carrying no billing context, as the sum reported them. In the figure only when the unclassified key is counted.

invoice_basis.description: The window's issued revenue under the applied recurring set. Null when no set applies — the card still asks.

contexts.description: One verdict per listed context, in the order `groups` lists them.

cadence.description: The cadence the context's billed months formed, or null when none did or the months could not be read.

missed_rule.description: Why the context is out: a cadence rule it missed ("one_month", "too_few_months", "irregular_gaps", "multiple_debits_in_month"), or "months_unreadable" when the rows carried no readable month for it. Null when it is in.

months_billed.description: The distinct months the context billed in, sorted, as YYYY-MM.

policy.description: The recurring rule the verdicts applied, in one line for the answer to restate.

recurring_contexts.description: The keys the cadence rule counted — the measured set itself, which a recorded pick can still outrank.

measured.description: The read's own cadence verdicts. Null on a refused read; always present on a successful one, partial included.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

next_step.description: What to do with the card this result renders. Added by the dispatcher when the card asks for a click.

partial.description: True when the aggregate behind these figures was cut short. Every amount is then a FLOOR rather than a measurement, and the recurring set is never settled by one.

party_scope.description: What the receivable side resolved to. `side_unknown: true` means the workspace resolved no own company, so NO side filter was applied (`applied: false`) and the list covers invoices on both sides — say the side is unknown, never that these are the contexts the workspace issued. `null` when the read reported no scope resolution.

recurring_contexts.description: The settled set: the keys the figure counts as recurring, applied as they stand when `reuse_stored_choice` is true. Empty when the card still asks — and also when the verdict is that nothing recurs, which `reuse_stored_choice` tells apart.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

reuse_stored_choice.description: True when the card asks nothing this call: the recurring set is already settled — by the pick this conversation recorded, or by the cadence the read measured. Apply `recurring_contexts` as they stand and wait for nothing. An empty set beside `true` is the verdict that nothing in the window recurs: say so plainly, never render a zero.

unreadable_rows.description: Invoices in the window whose net amount or currency could not be read. They are in no figure here, including the no-billing-context one. Null when the count could not be read.

title: List the billing contexts a reader can count as recurring
